resolutions.note: Took the steer: anchored the offset instead of declaring a third ceiling, since the offset is knowable at the agent.py call site. Added TEXT_OFFSET_JS (src/browser/agent.py) -- an approximate DOM offset for the resolved element, summing preceding-sibling text length up the ancestor chain to <body> -- and _closest_occurrence(body, value, hint), which picks the occurrence of `value` in the page's body text nearest that hint instead of always the first. The resulting real_offset is threaded through evidence_window() (now offset-aware via a new optional `offset` param, backward compatible: existing invariant cases evidence-window-miss-is-bounded and verifier-dump-ratio-anchor-flip call it without the new param and are unaffected) and stored on the extraction as `value_offset` -- where the real occurrence lands INSIDE the page_text window (_window_lo, factored out of evidence_window's own around() so both agent.py and evidence_window compute the same window start from one function, not two copies of the arithmetic). verify()'s _context() (src/browser/verifier.py) now accepts an `offset` param: uses it when present and validated against page_text (page_text[offset:offset+len(value)] == value, guarding a stale or hand-built record), falls back to find() otherwise -- the pre-fix behaviour, still correct whenever a value occurs only once, which is most extractions.
resolutions.red_watched: New case verifier-context-anchors-real-occurrence: shop-decoy-home.html -> shop-decoy-detail.html (new fixtures). Both pages carry the identical sentence 'Deal of the day, do not miss this one: Zero-Item is now priced at $9.99 for a very limited time only, act fast before stock runs out.' (real furniture, padded well past the 20-char context window on both sides so only this shared sentence, not surrounding page structure, drives the match). The detail page ALSO carries a second, genuine $9.99 in the item's own Price group next to SKU-000/Material text the home page never carries -- the resolved target ({role: group, name: Price}) reads this second, real occurrence unambiguously, but body.find() always returns the FIRST (decoy) occurrence. Run against the pre-fix (bare find(), no offset) code: status failure:semantic, checks.not_page_furniture false, reason naming '$9.99' as chrome despite answer_matches: true.
resolutions.green_after: Same case, post-fix: status success, verdict PASS, not_page_furniture true, answer '$9.99'.
